title: Magellan: A High-Performance Loop-Guided Prefetcher for Indirect Memory Access
problem: Graph analytics and sparse linear algebra applications rely heavily on indirect memory access (IMA), where pointer-chasing through irregular data structures causes frequent high-latency DRAM accesses due to poor temporal and spatial locality. Existing hardware and software prefetchers for IMA target narrow access patterns and struggle with complex nested-loop IMA patterns in sparse workloads.
motivation: Sparse applications dominate scientific and graph-analytics workloads, and their irregular memory access patterns stall processors waiting for DRAM at rates that hardware prefetchers cannot address due to limited look-ahead through pointer indirections.
method: Magellan is a compiler-based software prefetcher that analyzes pointer-chasing chains (like A[B[i]], where one result feeds into the next lookup) across nested loops. It builds a map of data dependencies spanning loop boundaries and inserts prefetch instructions scheduled to arrive ahead of when they're needed, based on how many times the loop runs and estimated memory fetch time. This approach covers multi-level indirection patterns that single-level prefetchers miss, prefetching for both current and future loop iterations.
key_novelty: Magellan is the first prefetcher to track data dependencies across multiple loop levels and understand how inner and outer loops interact to handle nested pointer-chasing patterns.
contributions: Dependence graph extraction across loop levels to detect complex multi-level indirect memory access patterns
Inner-outer loop semantic analysis to schedule prefetches for both current and future loop iterations
25% reduction in cache misses and 14% reduction in dynamic instruction count vs. best prior IMA software prefetcher
1.14x average speedup (up to 1.41x) across 14 memory-intensive benchmarks on real-world social network and web graph datasets

metrics.speedup: 1.14x average, up to 1.41x over best existing IMA software prefetcher
metrics.other: 25% cache miss reduction, 14% dynamic instruction count reduction

limitations: Evaluation is limited to CPU benchmarks; applicability to GPU-resident graph analytics or hardware prefetcher co-design is not discussed.
primary_theme: compiler-guided software prefetching for irregular memory access
